steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: He's not here?

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Mein Herr stepped out a while ago.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: He left?

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: He's off to the hospital just outside the Afterglow, to talk treatment for the Infected who got poisoned.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: What's this, Mein Herr? The hospital––

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I managed to twist the arms of the largest two and got them to sign contracts, but as for the rest... there's no hope.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But Rhodes Island signed an agreement with those hospitals!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Oh, I didn't notice you were here as well.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: There's no point. Rhodes Island's contracts are limited to symptoms caused by Oripathy itself. They have ample grounds to not treat Infected patients who've fallen ill from poisoning.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: But, Mein Herr, you got those two hospitals. That should be enough, right?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Hmph. Enough? Of course it's enough! I put every copyright I hold down as collateral, of course the consortium behind them thinks that's enough!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Don't tell me you– You transferred all your copyrights over to that consortium?!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I did. Not just the existing copyrights. I even sold the distribution rights for tomorrow's concert to them.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Now, I can start from scratch... *cough*, *cough*.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: *cough*... *cough*!

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Mein Herr?!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You're awake?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Urgh... Mhm...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Mr. Czerny, you didn't take any precautionary measures when you went out, did you?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You're talking about the fumes from those Originium slugs? I didn't waste a single second getting those contracts signed. That's all that mattered to me when I left.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Promise me you'll never be that reckless ever again.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: 'Ever again?' Are you saying, I still have time left to live?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: That's why I'm here.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Heh. You never want to see a doctor until your body gives out on you.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Thank you, Hibiscus.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I'm just doing my job.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: That reminds me, why haven't you said anything, Ebenholz? Are you thinking of throwing in the towel now that the Afterglow is too dangerous?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I'll tell you straight– now that we've come this far, the concert MUST go on. Don't even think about running.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Don't even think about running, huh...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (Whispers) Do you think he'd accept it now?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: (Whispers) Give it a moment...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Seems like you're not here to tell me you're quitting the concert?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No, I'm not here to tell you I'm quitting the concert.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Ebenholz, you repeat what others say when you get nervous. I've noticed it from the very beginning.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: If you have something to say, just spit it out. You think there's anything I wouldn't be able to accept in the state I'm in now?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: *cough* –– *cough* *cough* *cough*!!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Mr. Czerny, here, water!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: *cough*, *cough* *cough*... Damn–– damn that Gertrude!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: And you! How could you possibly go along with a plan like that? Curse me for thinking you had some creative talent, and this is what you use it for? Some evil plot?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It wasn't my intention––

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: How could it not be? Haven't you answered to that crazy woman from the very beginning?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Czerny, I still remember what you said. Even deeply-rooted hatred can still be pure music as long as it is expressed with the right technique.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I did say that, but what comes next? What are you trying to express?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: To be honest, I'm already starting to find my old way of thinking quite laughable.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But what I wish to pursue... is nothing more than freedom.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: ––Freedom. A longing for freedom, is it?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You've got a long way to go before you can express that using music!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: This has long been a deeply-rooted experience for me. Otherwise, I would not have come to you.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Come now.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Where are we going?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Where else? The concert hall.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Gertrude managed to keep me out of the lounge with her little tricks last time, but we're going to get to the bottom of this.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But, your health...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Instead of sitting here popping blood vessels over him and that woman, I might as well go see what they're up to.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Ebenholz, did Gertrude ever tell you if she did anything to the lounge?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: She didn't say anything.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: She doesn't have to say anything.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You can already tell?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Her fingerprints are all over this place...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: See that speaker right there? It shows obvious signs of having been dismantled. The same goes for the record player over there. She didn't even bother to tighten the screws–– Tsk, even the screwdriver's been left out in the open.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Just the kind of handiwork I'd expect from a noble. Hilarious.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Hibiscus, bring that record player over. Let's see what else has been tampered with besides the tonearm.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: See for yourself.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Did she just install an amplifier? That's only going to cause interference between the circuits...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: She already had the stylus removed. This thing's basically just an amplifier now.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Same with the speaker. The input circuit was completely removed and replaced with an amplifier... What is she trying to do putting so many amplifiers in the lounge?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: She never mentioned it.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Then let's give it a try. Go up on stage and play something. That'll be the fastest way to get our answer.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Doesn't seem like anything unusual is happening?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I can't hear anything out of the ordinary either.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Go over and tell Ebenholz to apply a little bit of Arts... Only the simplest kind to disperse drowsiness, maintained strictly at the lowest level.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: *cough*, *cough* *cough*, *cough*––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Czerny!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: *cough*, *cough*...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Don't worry about me... I just, got some palpitations, that's all...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Ebenholz, stand over here, and try using the same Arts as before. Remember to mind the volume.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: An echo?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: It's a sound coming from outside.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But isn't it the sound of Ebenholz's flute?
Czerny opens his mouth, but no voice comes out.
The answer already seems clear to him.
However, the expression Hibiscus sees on his face is not one of excitement or anger, but of terror.
Pure terror.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Gertrude converted this lounge, no, the entire Afterglow Hall, into a massive amplifier – an Arts amplification device.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: The amplifier stays off as long as it doesn't detect any musical Arts.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: But as soon as someone casts musical Arts, the amplification device activates... and exponentially amplifies the Arts as the music spreads through Afterglow Hall.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: The leakages and Resonanz of the Voice of Mundane... are no exception.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (Stares vacantly)

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: In other words, Originium activation will spike in all areas that are affected, meaning that everyone in Vyseheim, virtually without exception, will be infected...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: And those who already have Oripathy are even less likely to be spared. After they die, their bodies will rapidly disintegrate, releasing a large amount of active Originium microparticles...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: The surrounding area will be permanently poisoned, and Vyseheim will be completely cut off from the outside world––
Very sorry to interrupt your little chat, but I'm here to offer a suggestion.
Why cast Arts of wakefulness across all of Vyseheim on such a beautiful night? I often suffer from insomnia.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: My apologies, but we're dealing with something very important right now...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Gertrude?!

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Good evening, Czerny.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: And this must be Operator Hibiscus from Rhodes Island, yes? 'tis a pleasure to meet you.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: As for the young man in shock over there, why not come visit my home for something to drink? Perhaps have a nice night's rest, and return energized tomorrow?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Ger... Gertrude... To think you'd actually––

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I'd actually what? Don't tell me you're going to say that I'd actually deceive you and make you murder half the city?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: That can't be right.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: What you're actually mad about is how I had you running in circles, and nearly got you killed without you even noticing. Right?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Show us your pride as a noble, Graf Urtica. Come on, say something.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Ebenholz, she's trying to provoke you.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: There's only one thing I need to know from you right now: Why did you come here?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I came because you woke me up, why else?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I'll take that as, you heard the musical Arts rippling outwards and realized your plans had been discovered.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: That's correct.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Ahh, what a pity. With just one more day, I would've enjoyed a complete success.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Don't you think you should be thinking about how to escape? Do you seriously think your plan will proceed as normal if you manage to take us out here?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Ebenholz won't help you anymore, and regardless of what you were planning for the duet, it's not going to happen now!

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Really? That's not how I see it.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: As long as Ebenholz and Kreide are here, my plan has not failed.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: As long as I eliminate you, I can continue negotiating with Graf Urtica. He is quite familiar with the art of the noble dealings, and changing his mind is hardly an impossibility.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Most importantly, I don't think you lot can actually beat me.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: If the three of you were equal in power to Graf Urtica, then I certainly would have to watch my step. But you three, aha... Pardon my rudeness.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Don't waste your breath.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Graf Urtica, why don't we both take a step back? What do you say?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Take a step back?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I dismantle these giant amplifiers, and you continue working with me. That way, only Kreide has to die. Not a bad deal considering he only has a few days to live anyway, right?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: In your dreams.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: That truly is a shame. Due to unfortunate circumstances, you were forced to choose the path most ill-suited for you.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: If that is your heart's desire, then so be it. What a shame––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Shut up...

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: You'll regret this for the rest of your life.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I said, shut up!!

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: The time for talk is over. It seems we can only settle this with a fight.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: If I win, the self-appointed guardians of the Afterglow will have to behave themselves and keep their mouths shut so I can continue negotiating with Graf Urtica.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: If you win, then there's nothing more to say. A win is a win.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Take your wand out, Graf Urtica. Or do you plan to have those two Infected fight for you?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Like I said, your provocations won't get you anywhere.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hibiscus, stay out of this. Today, I swear I'll––

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Think carefully about where we are, and what's all around us!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Unless you're able to do this without any musical Arts, you'll drive all the inhabitants of Vyseheim insane before the disease ever comes!

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Tsk tsk. You're a quick thinker, Fräulein Hibiscus.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Since you caught on so quickly, I suppose there's no other choice but to take it outside.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Let me get this out there first. Rid yourself of the notion that escape counts as victory. While I personally dislike roughing up innocent bystanders, I can't say the same for my underlings.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You must not have a whole lot of confidence in yourself, based on how many you brought with you.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I'm so glad to hear your sharp wit once more. I'm almost moved to tears.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Are you feeling better now, Graf Urtica?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Of course, Dame Strollo.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Let's head outside and fight to our hearts' content.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: There must be nobody for you to spar with back in Urtica. Should be lonely, right?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: If I did, I wouldn't be playing with an old bag like you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: After all, you've never even challenged your own brother for his title. You have to wait for him to die before you can move up. I'm guessing you've never bested him in a fight before.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Very good, very good. I'm starting to hate you more and more.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The feeling is mutual.
